package http

import (
	"encoding/json"
	h "net/http"

	p "metaldocs/internal/platform/problem"
)

// A3.2 gate C3 negative fixture: the SAME forbidden serializer as
// local_problem_writer.go, reached through import aliases.
//
// The rule it breaks is about a shape — a function holding both the response
// writer and the problem value is a serializer — and a shape does not change
// when the author renames the packages it is spelled with. An analyzer keyed to
// the identifiers "http" and "problem" says otherwise: it hands anyone who
// writes `h "net/http"` a silent exemption from the one rule that keeps the API
// to a single error envelope. A guard a rename can turn off is advice, not a
// guard.
//
// So this file is deliberately narrower than its sibling. It never names
// "application/problem+json", which means the media-type rule cannot fire here
// and the finding it produces can only have come from the SIGNATURE rule
// resolving net/http and internal/platform/problem by import PATH. If a future
// edit went back to matching local identifiers, this file stops being reported,
// its Want line in tools/verify/registry.go stops appearing, and the fixture
// fails — which is how alias-independence stays a fact rather than a comment.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func writeAliasedProblem(w h.ResponseWriter, prob *p.Problem) {
	payload, err := json.Marshal(prob)
	if err != nil {
		w.WriteHeader(h.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}
	w.WriteHeader(prob.Status)
	_, _ = w.Write(payload)
}
